comments.body:
**Review and fix of the proof (issue first_proof_2-1).**

I read q2 (Nelson, Whittaker functions and Rankin-Selberg integrals) and the existing solution.tex. The overall strategy is correct and is the right idea:

- The required uniformity (W must be fixed before pi, while Q = generator of q^{-1} grows with the conductor) is handled by supporting W|_{P_{n+1}} on the *integral* mirabolic N_{n+1}(P_n cap K). On that set the embedded g has g_{nn}=1, so the only effect of u_Q on the integrand is multiplication by the unimodular constant psi(-Q). Thus W depends only on Pi, never on pi or Q.
- I numerically verified the key matrix identity diag(g,1).u_Q = (g, Q.g e_n), with (n,n+1)-entry = Q.g_{nn} (Lemma 1 / eq. twist).
- Lemmas 2 and 4 are the standard Bernstein-Zelevinsky/Kirillov facts: for an irreducible *generic* representation the Kirillov model contains C_c^inf(N_r\\P_r, psi) (highest derivative nonzero <=> generic), and the restriction to P_r is injective. These are correctly invoked.
- The non-vanishing M(V) != 0 reduces to prescribing V|_{P_n} = 1 on P_n cap K, giving M(V)=vol((N_n cap K)\\(P_n cap K))>0. Correct, and uses no information about the conductor of pi.

**Gap found and fixed.** Proposition (collapse) introduced a constant c_0 := vol((N_n cap K)\\N_n(P_n cap K)), an ill-matched quotient (it mixes the subgroup N_n cap K with the set N_n(P_n cap K)), and then 'absorbed the N_n-fibre volume' without justification. The conclusion (Psi = const.psi(-Q).M(V), const>0) was right, but the explicit constant was wrong/unjustified.

I rewrote the collapse step rigorously:
1. Psi(s,W,V) = int_{N_n\\N_n(P_n cap K)} psi(-Q) V(p) dgdot (support of integrand).
2. The inclusion P_n cap K -> N_n(P_n cap K) induces a homeomorphism (N_n cap K)\\(P_n cap K) ~= N_n\\N_n(P_n cap K), using N_n cap (P_n cap K)=N_n cap K and N_n-equivalence of every element to one in P_n cap K.
3. Transporting the invariant quotient measure gives a positive Radon measure dmu on the compact quotient; choosing the Haar normalizations so that dmu = dp yields Psi(s,W,V) = psi(-Q).M(V), independent of s. (Other normalizations only rescale by a fixed positive constant, changing nothing.) Removed c_0 throughout (overview, Theorem proof).

After this fix the chain is complete: Psi(s,W,V) = psi(-Q).M(V) is a fixed nonzero complex number (|psi(-Q)|=1, M(V)>0), independent of s, hence finite and nonzero for all s in C. The answer to the problem is **yes**.

LaTeX environment/brace balance checked (no toolchain available to compile). The proof in solution.tex is now, in my assessment, complete and rigorous, modulo the cited standard B-Z/Kirillov structure theorems.
